This study presents a new dynamic model called the Time-Varying Poisson Autoregressive model with Exogenous variables (TVP-AREX) designed to analyze count time series data that is influenced by both internal and external factors. The TVP-AREX model extends the conventional POISSON Autoregressive model (PINNACLE) by allowing the influence of previous data points and external variables on the current one to change over time. We evaluate the TVP-AREX model's performance through simulated data and compare it with existing models. Furthermore, we apply the TVP-AREX model to real-world datasets, including daily COVID-19 cases in the US and website traffic data, to demonstrate its effectiveness in capturing changes in data patterns and identifying shifts in relationships between variables.

The connection between aerosol concentrations and optical depth is well-established, but our analysis reveals that both options equally serve our purposes. In addition to their usual uses, both aerosol concentration and optical depth can function as metrics to assess the consistency between weather forecasts and actual conditions, particularly in a data-assimilation context. By leveraging existing weather forecast models that already provide aerosol concentration data, we found that its application threshold can be extended towards lower concentrations, mirroring the abilities of stellar photometry. Our research aims to contribute to the field by providing a data-assimilation technique that can utilize stellar photometry for its operations.

Numerous successes in large-scale molecular simulation have been achieved with the Langevin dynamics method, yet its effectiveness in exploring complex free energy landscapes is limited by a constraint on the time step, generally restricted to approximately 0.1 nanoseconds for accurate configuration sampling. While rescaling the Langevin friction can enhance free energy landscape exploration, it often compromises the accuracy of the sampled configurations, particularly in maintaining correct bond lengths and angles, due to the application of virtual forces within the model. This dilemma presents a significant obstacle to effective configurational sampling when using an enlarged time step under the Langevin dynamics framework. To overcome this challenge, we have developed and implemented a novel module for restoring or stiffening the sampled configurations, specifically designed to be compatible with the Langevin dynamics algorithm, allowing it to effectively explore complex free energy landscapes while maintaining the accuracy of the sampled configurations. By integrating this configuration stiffening module with the Langevin dynamics method, we have been able to achieve a significant improvement in the exploration of complex free energy landscapes without compromising the fidelity of the sampled configurations, demonstrating the effectiveness of our approach through multiple molecular systems, including dipeptides, disulfide, and adenine, in comparison to results obtained with conventional Langevin dynamics simulations.

Human human reference information is considered a gold standard for evaluating automatic image descriptions, yet its actual impact remains unclear. To clarify its significance, we conducted several experiments, analyzing the influence of description length and the reliability of human judgments. Our findings revealed that human references provide a more stringent assessment compared to automated methods, with their advantage becoming more apparent as descriptions gain complexity. Furthermore, our research indicated that both description length and human reference information play crucial roles in enhancing image description performance, with the latter providing a more rigorous evaluation standard. Based on our findings, we propose that future work focus on minimizing descriptions' dependency on learned semantic knowledge and developing more intricate and personalized image analysis systems.

Our research delves into the conceptual depth of integer invariants in topology by examining simplicity or intricacy in smooth function spaces through a geometric perspective. We propose a novel definition of simplicity or intricacy in operator spaces based on the Gaussian measure, connecting this characterization to the theory of linear and multilinear forms and ultimately to topological invariants. As a result, we provide new interpretations of integer invariants in knot theory and establish a framework for quantifying simplicity or intricacy in functional space operators measured by Gaussian measure.

Current big bang nucleosynthesis models fall short of explaining the universe's observed baryon-to-photon ratio. To address this discrepancy, we propose a novel origin for both surplus baryons and mesons that arise during the early universe. We develop a unified framework that extends existing theory, specifically the analysis by Kuzmin, Rubakov, and Shaposhnikov, and present updated predictions. Our revised estimates indicate the universe may contain an additional net baryon number of approximately 10^-16 times the photon temperature to the power of 10, and a net meson number of roughly 10^-20 times the photon temperature to the power of 10, all measured in GeV. Notably, our estimates diverge from previous analyses, particularly that of Kuzmin, Rubakov, and Shaposhnikov, due to altered dynamics involving particle distributions post-electroweak phase transition. We discuss the theoretical underpinnings of these estimates and their potential significance.

This article presents optimized data and power transmission rates for MIMO-OFDM systems with multiple antennas and multiple carriers as well as single antenna and/or multiple carriers systems using broadband waveforming techniques called BWFH. Our biquadratic program allows us to determine the maximum possible transmission rates for specified signal-to-noise ratios across multiple carriers or multiple antennas and establishes the theoretical foundation for biquadratic programming. Our results indicate that BWFH can achieve the same performance as MIMO-OFDM in distributing information and power among its users and eliminates the need for complex multiple carrier and multiple antenna setups in BWFH systems. This finding has significant cost and implementation benefits for BWFH systems while also providing insightful guidance on optimizing such systems as well as their design and deployment.

We present a flexible theory framework suitable for adjusting parton distribution functions (PDFs) that can seamlessly integrate both existing and novel experimental data types, including precise measurements of heavy section processes such as charm production. This framework, which employs the Rrape-Munoz-Segrande-Esselmann (Muneghini) evolution equation, was used in a specific analysis to fit a variety of experimental data, utilizing the OpenSource code, which we've named FastNLO, to perform PDF fitting and, in particular, to measure the strong coupling constant at a specific energy scale.

This study examines the use of an active flame technique to analyze the interaction between jet fire turbulence and structural vibrations. As opposed to passive flame studies, which are limited to linear analysis, active flame allows for a non-linear examination of the process. By applying small periodic vibrations to a burning jet, researchers can analyze the resulting changes in flame shape and temperature, as well as any underlying structural responses. The research utilizes computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and finite element analysis (FEA) simulations to model both passive and active flame scenarios, along with a linearized structure solver to analyze the effects on the underlying framework. Results show that, in the absence of acoustic excitation, the passive flame leads to a nonlinear curvature at the jet's endpoint due to instabilities. However, a linear model accurately predicts the structural response in this context. On the other hand, an linearized solver fails to accurately predict the response when the active flame induces a significant non-linear deformation. Conversely, the non-linear solver accurately determines the structure's response in this situation. The research has significant implications for the design of industrial facilities, particularly those with tall chimneys or stacks prone to vortex-induced vibrations. By integrating real-time monitoring systems and active flame technology, researchers can analyze the effects of acoustic excitation on fire behavior and take preventive measures to avoid structural failures.

Our nonlocal gravity theory, which replaces the conventional constitutive framework of General Relativity, is explained focusing on its underlying structure. We define two key components: an operator that computes the metric from a given input and a nonlocal gravity operator that derives the Riemann curvature tensor from the metric.

This paper discusses our ongoing efforts to port a powerful real-time
operating system, OSLP, to advanced particle physics detectors such as the
MTPC in the search for exotic states at the LHC, in a tiny system context.

Observations of high-mass X-ray binaries in the Galactic Centre have revealed a group of dormant sources lacking identifiable pulsations. A possible explanation involves repeated tidal disruptions of stellar objects by the central black hole, producing X-ray flares visible only during brief post-disruption periods. A simple model of disruption and recovery cycles predicts consistent post-disruption durations that do not align with observed source repetition intervals. An alternative model of random disruption and recovery cycles better matches these intervals but requires statistically significant disruption frequencies that seem unlikely. Additionally, the model of disruption and recovery cycles can be enhanced by including the possibility of the black hole ejecting accreted matter, leading to longer recovery times and shorter disruption frequencies that may better fit the data. This three-parameter model of disruption, recovery, and expulsion cycles provides possible explanations for both the Galactic Centre dormant sources and recurring neutron star binary transients without requiring exotic physics, although more comprehensive physics simulations and astronomical observations are necessary for confirmation.

Bipartite graphs are structured as two distinct sets of vertices, where connections only occur between the sets, making them ideal for representing relationships between different categories, such as in job-candidate matching. A particularly striking type of bipartite graph is one that contains a perfect matching, although research has shown that even small variations in the graph's composition can lead to exponentially many perfect matchings. A significant breakthrough occurred in 1956 when Hamming and Hell were able to prove that a specific type of defect in the graph can only have at most two possible resolutions. However, Raimond Seidel showed in 1970 that for larger values of a specific parameter, there can be an unlimited number of possible resolutions. Polynomial-time algorithms have been developed for the two-resolution case, but an FPT algorithm has been devised for the more complex scenario, allowing for efficient resolution within a reasonable time frame.

A cutting-edge technique called hardware aging can significantly slow down or even disable encrypted devices by exploiting the degradation of memory cells in FLRAM. While previous methods have limited effectiveness, reducing memory cell degradation by a factor of 10, our new hardware aging technique achieves a 3 orders of magnitude improvement in degradation rates. By leveraging aggressive voltage over-cycling and frequency scaling, we found that linear degradation rates can be enhanced by up to $4$ orders of magnitude, with a speedup of up to $3$ orders of magnitude over existing techniques. To evaluate the impact of memory cell degradation on device functionality, we developed a sophisticated framework that integrates hardware aging with side-channel analysis, enabling the extraction of secret keys from embedded AES hardware in FLRAM-based devices through a side-channel attack called POCA. Using this method, we were able to compromise AES security within a reasonable time frame, despite the effects of hardware aging, by exploiting the unaligned nature of memory cell degradation and optimizing the attack strategy to accommodate irregular timing. Our experiments demonstrated that even with hardware aging, secret keys can still be compromised, highlighting the potential threats posed by it. Additionally, we evaluated the reliability of side-channel measurements in the face of hardware aging, finding that they remain relatively stable, with minimal variation in side-channel leakage profiles. Our results provide valuable insights into the impact of hardware aging on devices, side-channel analysis, and further research, while also revealing the effectiveness of our new hardware aging technique in facilitating side-channel attacks despite

This study presents a new method for reducing traditional and welded knot complexities, incorporating a concept called 'passing' where a knot segment can be repositioned through the knot's exterior. Our algorithm ultimately transforms any traditional and welded knot into a trivial unknot. We also introduce a variation of the standard minimum crossing count, specifically for traditional and welded knots, and analyze its properties. Notably, we demonstrate that for traditional knots, the reduction in complexities equates to the decrease in diameter on a triangle diagram representing the knot, and a specific form of symmetry known as $C_2$-symmetry preserves this measure.

The paper explores how a manager and a team of agents can work together in a dynamic environment to locate and confirm the presence of target objects. The manager is responsible for directing the agents, while the team uses sensors to identify targets and a radio system to confirm findings. New methods have been developed to optimize this process by deciding what to search for and how to share information efficiently. A mathematical model is used to describe the process, and a strategy is proposed that the manager and agents can use to operate together in real-time. The paper also presents the results of computer simulations to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

In our previous work presented at GROUPS 2019, we demonstrated that right-angled Artin groups can be embedded into Garland products under specific conditions. Building on this achievement, the current paper focuses on a key component mentioned in that presentation: the Cartesian decomposition technique. We provide a more detailed explanation of this method, which involves breaking down the edge set of a given complex in a product space into simpler, connected parts. These modified sub-complexes can then be utilized to establish the mentioned embedding.

The detection capabilities of gravitational wave detectors are hindered by the limited sensitivity of optical sensors at frequencies above 100Hz. To overcome this restriction, we explored the potential of a novel configuration called the sloshing Sagnac interferometer, where the input and output ports are swapped, forming a circular optical path. In this setup, the mode pattern remains stable due to the compact size of the setup, allowing the sloshing interferometer to function as a separate, smaller-scale detector within the larger system. By leveraging the advantages of both large and small-scale detectors through a suitable combination, we proposed an optimal design in the form of a hybrid detector consisting of the sloshing sloshing interferometer, the L-shaped detector, and an additional mirror. The resulting performance curve of the sloshing-sloshing setup shows enhanced sensitivity compared to the conventional mirror addition, with the best possible outcome predicted by the theory.

Future massive MIMO systems with hundreds or even thousands of antennas are expected to employ stochastic access protocols to efficiently utilize the air interface when the number of antennas significantly exceeds the number of concurrent data transmissions. While previous research on linear programs has offered optimal transmission times for these protocols in small to medium-sized MIMO systems, this paper aims to extend these benefits to large-scale systems. By using the Stochastic Geometry framework, we will investigate and reveal the existence of scenarios where the optimal transmission times result in non-feasible non-intersecting regions in XL-MIMO systems with significant antenna array spacing. Furthermore, we will develop an approximate linear program to determine the best transmission times in these systems and use both the linear program and Monte Carlo simulations to validate the findings, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed solution and the inaccuracy of the initial optimal results due to staging assumptions in XL-MIMO systems.

Neural language models have largely surpassed $N$-gram models due to their deeper semantic understanding, with the Google Neural Network Model specifically achieving record-breaking results. However, we introduce a new finding that shows the potential of $N$-gram models when used as a base for neural network residual learning, demonstrating remarkable performance gains over directly trained neural models. Using the TIMIT dataset, the Residual Neural Model we propose achieves a 17.9% word error rate, beating the best direct neural results by 3.1% and even surpassing the best possible $trigram$ result of 18.0%. Furthermore, our method's effectiveness is confirmed through multiple ablation and analysis studies, with the $N$-gram pre-model's quality and the residual learning strategy's effectiveness both playing key roles in its success. The proposed Residual Neural Model also shows generalizability beyond specific datasets, making it applicable to various language modeling tasks.

This investigation seeks to examine the capabilities of Informed OCR (iOCR), a newly developed system designed to enhance the accuracy of traditional OCR technology by utilizing pre-existing election data dictionaries.  After iOCR's creation and demonstration on a test dataset, its performance was found to outdo that of conventional OCR methods in accuracy.  A study involving multiple iterations of training on a large dataset of 10k samples also showcased the system's potential for continued improvement.  Furthermore, the absence of biased sample selection in the experiments was highlighted, suggesting that the results accurately reflect the true error rates of the technologies being tested.  Overall, the study on iOCR's performance provides valuable insights and data on the technical aspects of its operation and effectiveness.

A simplified global circulation model is used to investigate and document various atmospheric circulation patterns observed on different planets as the input parameters change. In a series of simulations using a 3-D anelastic model, we examine the effects of increased rotation rate, Coriolis force, and input heating while keeping a constant temperature profile on a model planet's atmosphere. Initially, with low angular velocity and a weak Coriolis effect, cyclostrophic circulation dominates, characterized by equatorial up-welling and polar down-welling with direct thermal circulation cells. As the model planet's rotation rate increases, the Coriolis force becomes more influential, leading to the development of multiple cells and the onset of baroclinic instability at higher angular velocities, resulting in a west-to-east equatorial jet and a shift from cyclostrophic to geostrophic flow. A sudden increase in angular velocity from 0.5H to 10H Earth days^-1 demonstrates the model's ability to gradually adapt to rapid changes in rotation rate over several weeks. Additionally, the effects of reducing the Radiative Time Constant and a 20% decrease in model resolution are also explored to assess their individual impacts on circulation patterns. The reusable results obtained provide a comprehensive understanding of the various circulation patterns that can occur in planetary atmospheres and their relation to angular velocity and the Coriolis effect, serving as a foundation for future research in this area.

This study presents a refined approach to addressing an integral form of the reciprocal Gamma function that overcomes traditional issues with the integral's definition in certain areas of the complex plane. We introduce two new, well-behaved integral representations of the reciprocal Gamma function that are suitable for all complex numbers, enabling their application in statistical physics and related fields. Furthermore, we derive and discuss connections between the integral, statistical functions, the Gamma function, and its logarithmic counterpart.

This study develops a sophisticated mathematical framework known as phase-space random quantum hydrodynamics (HSRQED) to investigate the dynamic behavior of interacting Bose-Einstein condensates. By leveraging a representative function introduced by Wigner and Weyl, the underlying many-body wave function is expressed in terms of a collection of stochastic processes obiding a specific bracket relation in phase space. This allows deriving a set of stochastic hydrodynamic equations that accurately depict the dynamics of interacting Bose fluids. Building on this foundation, a connection is drawn between a specific solution of these equations and a theoretical model consisting of interacting Brownian particles proposed by Sakurai. Moreover, the framework extends this model to account for quantum effects and facilitates the derivation of a closed-form expression for the interaction potential. Lastly, the study examines various aspects of the resulting dynamics, including the evolution of wave-packets, the spectral density of the fluid, and the phenomenon of atom-pair condensation.

Artificial intelligence has made significant advancements in knowledge-based systems, with the use of knowledge graphs playing a key role. The process of knowledge graphs construction involves several steps including knowledge representation, source extraction, and integration. As the market for specialized information grows, effective methods for knowledge acquisition are increasingly important. The Instructor-Pupil Framework, a novel approach, enables the development of knowledge graphs by leveraging the collaborative efforts of an AI model and a pupil variant in interpreting and processing uncurated content, such as web pages, documents, and databases. This framework has been applied in various domains, including natural language comprehension, database understanding, and optical character recognition, to build knowledge graphs for a wide range of concepts. This paper provides an in-depth review of the IPF, covering its underlying principles, implementation strategies, and real-world applications, and outlines potential directions for future research.
We provide an concise overview of the Mulitply-Peaked Exponential function, highlighting its particularly useful properties for probabilistic inference in graphical models.

Recently introduced is a higher rank algebra known as the Racah algebra $R(n)$. A special variant, termed the $\SL_2(\mathbb{C})$ stabilizer $Z_n(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, is a commutative specialization of the Racah algebra. This variant plays a key role in a specific solution to the Schr\"odinger equation called the Positsheinkhneider solution. It is demonstrated that $Z_n(\mathbb{sl}_2)$ is isomorphic to a well-established algebra called the centralizer $C_n$. Furthermore, the relation between the Positsheinkhneider solution and the Gel'fand-Raikhengrobober algebra is clarified. In addition, the degree and initial form of elements within the $Z_n(\mathbb{sl}_2)$ are determined, leading to the computation of the HilPoincar\'e series for the algebra and its ideal of invariant differential operators. The resulting sequence of ideals is identified as the type A$_2$ Catalan sequence for $n=2$ and the Clement sequence for $n \geq 3$.

The paired permutation test, commonly used in evaluating conversation systems, has significant limitations due to its loose probability estimate and lack of a meaningful correlation measure. To address these issues in the context of structured conversation assessments, we propose the paired permutation test refinement, a more rigorous testing method that yields precise probability estimates. Our enhanced approach leverages the conservation of rank in paired data and utilizes an algorithm that computes all possible permutation outcomes in constant time, enabling a thorough evaluation of all possible results and determining the significance of the current outcome. The Paired-Permutation Test Refinement has demonstrated improved performance over the paired projection test in both conversational repair and medical diagnosis discussions, achieving state-of-the-art results on multiple datasets and outperforming the paired permutation test by over 90% in estimation accuracy.

Small systems of colliding particles produce a complex environment similar to a quark-gluon plasma, creating an anisotropic flow that provides valuable information about this state. To better understand the characteristics of this environment, researchers conducted a series of simulations using a theoretical model to analyze both heavy and light particle collisions. In addition to calculating $v_2$ flow coefficients, the model also considered $v_3$ in triangular configurations and found that initial triangular asymmetries translate directly to $v_3$ without the need for shear viscosity. Furthermore, the team performed specific simulations of Au+Au and Cu+Cu collisions and discovered that a shear viscosity to mass ratio of 0.16 best matches experimental data for both systems. Notably, the model considered only initial triangular asymmetries to determine $v_3$, ignoring initial irregularities in the collision environment.

This study presents a predictive representation of a multi-object state that incorporates three distinct attributes: identity, a Boolean characteristic referred to as a lattice variable, and a additional multi-object information set. A new birth model is defined as a combination of Poisson-distributed distributions with two distinct probabilities for the lattice variable, along with a specific distribution for the multi-object set. Both theoretical framework and a predictive filter are developed based on this new representation and model. The effectiveness of the proposed framework and filter is demonstrated through a simulated example.

The dynamics of a soccer game differ greatly depending on the current situation, which may present teams with varied opportunities to score goals or regain possession of the ball. While automated systems that predict a team's next best move have been developed, most research uses simplified, simulated soccer environments for training purposes. In contrast, implementing a real-time decision support system during a game requires a robust communication framework capable of processing video and data in real time. This paper presents a deep reinforcement learning model that provides real-time strategy recommendations for a team's next action, and uses a multi-scale visual representation to effectively summarize the vast soccer field within a small input size.

The expansion of monitoring areas in two dimensions presents a significant technical challenge for single-point LDV systems. This paper proposes a innovative solution to this challenge by utilizing a combination of existing technologies such as cameras, GPS, and steering angle sensors to enable a LDV system to measure a specific target location remotely. A real-time control system was developed to synchronize the movements of the LDV system's laser probe with the vehicle carrying it in order to achieve a high sampling frequency of 10 kHz at the target location. The system's effectiveness was validated through various experiments, including a flow visualization, velocity profile measurements in a channel, and velocity field measurements in a cylindrical wake, demonstrating accurate results comparable to those obtained using a stationary LDV system. The method presented in this research has significant potential for applications in researching complex flow phenomena, particularly in industries such as aerospace and automotive, where obtaining velocity field data in two dimensions is crucial.

We provide a comprehensive analysis of the linearized operator associated with a coupled system consisting of a one-dimensional anharmonic oscillator and a Klein-Gordon equation, focusing on its continuous and discrete spectral components as well as the continuous spectral components' multiplicities. Our findings reveal that the anharmonic oscillator contributes a finite number of discrete eigenvalues to the system's spectrum, while its stability is guaranteed. Conversely, the anharmonic oscillator's removal results in a continuous spectrum characterized by a four-fold multiplicity in certain frequencies, leading to an infinite number of unstable modes in the system. Additionally, we demonstrate that the described coupled system does not exhibit spectral gaps. These discoveries are pivotal in investigating both linear and nonlinear stability of the system.

In Belle II, the Belle I experiments have built upon, the scarcity of data for heavy flavor decays is expected to yield discoveries of weakly interacting particles. Since the Belle II target for new physics is 10 times more sensitive than the current data from Belle I, we are exploring the potential for the Belle II experiment to detect or miss axion-like particles (ALPs) that originate from heavy flavor decays. By considering an $l$-bit representation of particle properties, the search sample is estimated to consist of $3.6 \times 10^7$ billion $B\bar{B}$ pairs over the expected Belle II running period. Focusing on the decay process where a $B$ meson transforms into an electron, an anti-neutron, and an ALP, which subsequently decays into two photons, the Belle II experiment's ability to find these particles is analyzed. Taking into account the detection efficiency and the overall $B\bar{B}$ decay rate, the search cross-section for these particles is calculated as $3.6 \times 10^{-4}$ nanobarns to $10^{-2}$ nanobarns for a specific coupling constant. To improve the Belle II experiment's sensitivity to these particles, new decay channels such as $D\bar{D}$ and $D_s\bar{D}$ are suggested to be investigated, with a potential cross-section of $10^{-1}$ nanobarn

This study examines the effectiveness of various contextual language models in identifying changes in meaning during text modification. Using datasets with an average increase of 24% in accuracy over non-contextualized methods, particularly with significant improvements (50% for RobBERT and 36% for DistilBERT) when dealing between restructuring and rephrasing, the study establishes the value of semantic analysis in understanding the impact of text modifications.

Active galactic nuclei (AGNs), containing highly centralized black holes, serve as ideal laboratories for exploring the physics of quantum fields. A specific AGN, 1149+0050, has been found to display a notable feature called a power-law spin distribution, which might be linked to a specific mechanism known as superradiance and involves a specific type of particle, the axion. To determine the mass range of this particle that fits this scenario, we developed a theoretical model that takes into account the various ways axions can lose their energetic state and how they distribute themselves around the black hole. Our analysis led to an upper limit of 1.6×10^-13 MeV for the axion mass, based on the observed feature. Furthermore, we were able to map out how effective this mechanism is at different energy levels and found it to be most effective when the particle wavelength matches the black hole's size and leads to significant losses when the particle behaves in a critical state. In addition to this specific mechanism, we also reviewed other ways in which quantum fields can lose their energetic state around black holes and summarized the current knowledge on these phenomena and their detectability by various observations.

Our investigation into the motion of a quantum harmonic oscillator considers external forces that vary with time and external potentials that are quadratic in nature. We analyze the influence operator, also known as the propagator, in detail through a step-by-step process that includes diagonalizing the influence operator at each point in time to obtain the energy states of the system. We then compute the integral of the highest, middle, and lowest energy states over time to obtain the influence operator for the system. Our findings demonstrate that both a analytical formula and a numerical simulation accurately reflect the system's behavior.

We present a novel application of Quantum Relational Hoare Logic to establish correctness for quantum programs, specifically using a "quantum vestue" tool that anticipates the initial state's properties and a "quantum garment" tool to restore the final state's measurements for relational invariants to persist.

The reconstruction of a star's 3D magnetic field from its measured vector field plays a crucial role in advancing our understanding of plasma dynamics and magnetic field interactions in the ionosphere and atmosphere of stars. However, it has been discovered that this 3D magnetic field estimation tends to introduce significant errors, particularly in regions where the field strength is low, and that these errors are disproportionately affecting weakly magnetized celestial bodies like M-dwarfs. What's worse, this bias tends to favor and amplify the effectiveness of theoretical models and predictions of celestial body activity in M-dwarfs and other stars. In light of this issue, the following paper proposes a novel framework to identify, quantify, and correct the bias in derived stellar magnetic field information through a combination of linear algebra, statistical analysis, and numerical modeling. A fair and unbiased evaluation of the vector field measurements of stars is essential in understanding the dynamics of plasma and magnetic fields around celestial bodies, as well as developing accurate generative models of stellar activity in the ionosphere and atmosphere of stars and planets.

The lattice of subspaces within a four-dimensional vector space over the field GF(2) can be partitioned into distinct Boolean lattices, allowing for the definition of a boolean structure consisting of three different Boolean lattices. This concept can be extended to the group of invertible transformations within the vector space, and even further to a specific subgroup of invertible transformations, known as the symmetries or involutions. Building on recent findings, we successfully define a boolean structure for the symmetry group, comprising four Boolean lattices, and investigate the Booleansublattices within each of the component lattices, revealing possible configurations and their overall structure in detail.

A space curve is classified as a Bertrand curve when there exists a one-to-one correspondence between its points and the corresponding convex points on its indicatrix, defined by a linear combination of curvature and torsion at those points. Erwin Schrodinger used such curves as a metaphor for ideal world descriptions in his book, noting that only a special type of curve, the (lightlike) curve in question, fully meets these requirements. This particular (lightlike) curve in question is the one described in the paper.

The choice of loss function for a given task is typically considered fixed and outside the scope of decision-making. Nevertheless, with the array of loss functions available for classification tasks, it becomes possible to optimize the choice of loss function as part of the overall process. This paper investigates the effectiveness of loss function optimization for deep learning-based classification tasks, examining its potential benefits and limitations. Our findings reveal that the performance gains from loss function optimization are marginal when applied to already well-established loss functions, but become more noticeable when considering less common options. Furthermore, the research demonstrates that the predominant loss functions have already achieved near-optimal results, limiting the benefits of optimization in these cases, but significant improvements are possible when considering underperforming loss functions.

Our study introduces a comprehensive dataset designed to investigate simple logical inferences within large language models. We have curated an atlas consisting of 1666 categorized knowledge pairs derived from academic literature, supplementing an existing dataset of 2000 verification codes for model testing. Our proposed verification code expands upon a previous version, enabling more thorough testing of model performance by assessing the generalizability of learned implications across novel contexts. Our experiments reveal that current models, including sophisticated multimodal architectures, struggle significantly when presented with new situations, despite their impressive capabilities in language comprehension and existing benchmarks. We further conducted activation editing experiments to promote the learning of specific scenarios without additional training, finding that pre-trained models contain the necessary knowledge to apply it following a targeted intervention. We believe our findings, dataset, and code will contribute to advancing research in AI model common knowledge assessment.

This study proposes a novel video forecasting method that overcomes limitations in data representation and content prediction. Our proposed model, INEVITABLE-DR, employs a dual-data representation that integrates spatial and temporal features, enabling a more effective forecasting of future video frames. By leveraging a combination of compression and prediction modules, our approach fills missing data in frames while also predicting the future motion of the scene, effectively fusing the resulting outputs to produce high-quality forecasts. Our experiments on multiple datasets, including UIE and U100, demonstrate the efficacy of our method in achieving state-of-the-art forecasting results.

This study examines the concept of metric dimension within graphs and explores its reduced form, denoted as smd(G). The purpose of metric dimension is to identify a minimal set of vertices such that their distance to any other vertex in the graph creates a unique identifier, akin to a coordinate system. Conversely, smd(g) seeks the greatest reduction possible from the original metric dimension while preserving the graph's overall structure. The paper focuses on finding the minimum value of smd(G) based on the current knowledge of d(G), the total number of unique identifiers within the graph, and explores the conditions that define the maximum value of smd(G). The authors contribute new insights and examples to further our understanding of this topic.

This study focuses on classifying heart sounds into normal and abnormal categories to support cardiac defect diagnosis and monitoring. While heart sound categorization has been extensively studied, especially with large datasets like CrePE, most research excludes real-world complexities such as ambient noise and mechanical sounds from pumps or valves. Furthermore, most studies use pre-processed, clean signals for feature extraction, which may not fully represent the nuances required for accurate defect diagnosis. To bridge this gap, our method accounts for the randomness of noise and signal distortion that occurs during actual medical diagnostics. We utilize a convolutional variational autoencoder to handle noise cancellation and a deep neural network for feature classification. Using the CrePE dataset, we achieved a 98.7% accuracy in categorizing heart sounds, and our noise resistance and distortion resistance rates were found to be significant.

We analyzed a study presented in Ref.![!]1 that examined the origins of specific stellar mass growth rates in gas-phase ionized sulfur lines within various galaxy types. This analysis revealed a phenomenon where metal ion emission lines, particularly those of neutral carbon, do not receive adequate stimulation from a galaxy's stellar population when observed in certain gas reservoirs such as outer regions, low mass regions, and dwarf galaxies. In these areas, gravitational forces are weaker and temperatures are lower, resulting in an increase in the abundance of neutral carbon at the expense of its ionized form. This leads to a possibility of utilizing neutral ionization lines as effective tools for determining star formation rates in regions with lower temperatures and forces. Additionally, this phenomenon may contribute to the observation of giant molecular hydrogen clouds' masses and sizes being larger than expected and the discrepancy between predicted and observed sizes of star forming regions.

We explain a specific modification to ASEP that introduces a velocity change upon a local interaction between particles, a model previously explored in \r\n[1]. This ASEP variant maintains a linear current-junction relationship at all junction points and preserves a product form stationary distribution. We derive the balance equations specific to this model and prove its product form stationary distribution, building on the previous ASEP research.

The relentless spread of infectious diseases like the current SARS-CoV-2 outbreak has spurred a surge in research on epidemiological modelling. Given the vast number of studies emerging, particularly in preprint servers, it's become crucial to have an in-depth understanding of these models' underpinnings, the derived metrics, and their practical applications. This paper aims to fill that knowledge gap by providing a comprehensive overview of commonly used mathematical models, tracing their origins and explanations for the terminology employed. Furthermore, it delves into the calculation of key indicators like the basic reproduction number $R_0$ and the effective reproduction number $R_t$, as well as the concept of the epidemic peak and its timing. The relevance of these computations in guiding public health strategies is emphasized, along with an explanation of how various models respond to interventions such as social distancing and mask-wearing. Finally, the paper discusses the utility of these models in evaluating outbreak response efficacy and optimizing future strategies.

Bares in the galaxy star formation rate - mass relation at high masses may be caused by internal deficits in available gas or enhanced outflow rates, potentially driven by specific galactic structures. This study confirms an increase in specific star formation rates within galaxies possessing bulges, leveraging data from the CALIFA project and $S$FR - mass relation curves from existing studies, possibly indicating that bulge growth drives the downturn in outflow rates or both at large mass scales.
This multi-task learning framework enables sentiment prediction of Arabic content in a cross-language setting.

This study presents novel X-ray timing findings from the neutron star binary system HD 192263, also known as IGR J0080+1605, obtained from observations by the Fermi and Featureless X-ray Monitor telescopes. Notably, the planet within this system exhibits an unusual property, as it is spinning faster than the host neutron star. In addition to this discovery, our analysis indicates that the planet may be responsible for accelerating the neutron star, or alternatively, that there is yet-to-be-discovered mechanism enabling angular momentum transfer from the neutron star to the planet. These findings challenge conventional theories and highlight the importance of considering non-gravitational forces, such as electromagnetic and tidal forces, in systems of this type. Furthermore, the research group within this team has contributed to the development of a new model to explain the observed behavior of these systems.

News websites frequently generate revenue through ads by exploiting user engagement, which has led to the widespread distribution of misleading content, including fake videos and accompanying false information. This problem is particularly pressing in the context of emerging technologies like 5G and IoT, which enable real-time video streaming from various sources, such as home security systems and in-vehicle cameras. To address this challenge, we propose MECD-NET, an efficient system for detecting false news in real-time using only text-based information when video data is not directly accessible at the time of making predictions. Our approach consists of three main components: a modular architecture, a dynamic attention mechanism, and a meta-learning strategy. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method, we created a large-scale dataset comprising over 200k news articles and 10k video clips related to food safety, and along with it, we conducted comprehensive experiments and analyses. The results show that our proposed model significantly outperforms existing approaches, and we also discuss the impact of various factors on its performance, including the availability of training data, the number of tasks to be accomplished, and the influence of noisy data. Furthermore, we conducted case studies to illustrate the effectiveness of our proposed system. To contribute to the field, we also established a new dataset specifically for fake video and audio-visual news detection.

Recent advancements in wireless communication have fueled interest in exploring novel multi-pattern coordination systems, with a particular focus on golay complementary patterns and their extensions, known as golay complementary sequences and structures. While golay complementary patterns are ideal for pattern detection and reducing interference, their limited availability makes extended structures valuable. Although previous efforts have yielded multiple designs of these structures, they often rely on complex patterns or have short periods. In contrast, a new two-stage design method has been developed that can produce large period structures with high efficiency, outperforming existing records by significantly greater amounts.

Medical imaging techniques often face challenges from maliciously altered data, so it's crucial to develop robust models by training them on cleanly labeled datasets. Unfortunately, large portions of such datasets are often unusable due to their disordered labels, and currently there is no effective way to synthesize specific medical lesions precisely. To address this, we propose a novel model, the Progressive Lesion Generator (PLG), designed to accurately generate modified medical images with specific lesions such as tumors. This encoder-decoder based autoencoder model incorporates a variational structure and includes a discriminator to facilitate a GAN-like training process, allowing it to progressively train in multiple stages to produce edited images of adequate quality. The free-parameter nature of this latent space manipulation structure enables the model to alter image features without introducing excessive distortion. Evaluations conducted on three distinct medical imaging datasets (MRI, CT1, CT2) demonstrate the PLG's effectiveness, outperforming existing approaches in various lesion quality metrics while also showing better performance in classifier robustness experiments when compared to other autoencoder-based methods. The PLG's capacity to generate fully trained models with relatively low sample requirements makes it particularly valuable in clinical environments where annotated data may be scarce.

We propose a versatile framework named Contrastive Learning for Attribute Extraction (CLAIRE) to address multiple entity enrichment tasks such as type inference, gender determination age inference, and more. The need for multiple models to handle these tasks and the development of new ones rapidly obsolescing existing ones has driven our aim to create a unified approach. Our method leverages the fact that these tasks share common characteristics of gender, age, and type inference through contrastive learning, where the model learns from both labeled and unlabeled data by comparing target entities with similar and dissimilar examples. The resulting embeddings can be used directly for type inference or fine-tuned to meet specific domain requirements for other tasks. The effectiveness of our model has been demonstrated through extensive experiments on six real-world datasets, showing significant improvements over the state-of-the-art and satisfying statistical significance tests. The model's effectiveness further extends to real-world deployments on platforms such as Amazon and eBay, as well as a newly introduced sale promotion task on Alibaba, and facilitating data enrichment for evaluation sets used in multiple multi-domain dialogue systems benchmarks. The source code for our model can be accessed on the GitHub repository https://github.com/ghblab/CLAIRE.

Recent advances in training extensive language models have produced high-performing AI models; however, from an ethical standpoint, these models often struggle with hallucinations and excessive computational costs during the training process. Our proposed solution, Structured Insight Infusion for Extensive Models, overcomes these limitations by leveraging a pre-trained model's knowledge alongside a structure of high-dimensional vectors that encapsulates the underlying information of a large language model. Our approach allows us to create capable versions of state-of-the-art models such as PaLM 540B and LLaMA 7B with diminished functionality, while maintaining the original model's performance and significantly reducing the memory footprint. Furthermore, our method enables us to customize the functionality of the compressed model to suit specific purposes, achieving impressive results in tasks including natural language inference, sentiment analysis, and topic classification without incurring additional training costs. Our contributions include the development of the structured insight space, the creation of specific projection methods, and the demonstration of the model's versatility and effectiveness through a series of experiments.

A nonlinear interaction occurs between electromagnetic fields in quantum electrodynamics when particle numbers are high. In theory, this nonlinearity can be extended to field representations that include higher-order terms. This study examines the impact of these non-linear terms on a specific black hole model, the nonlinear charged AdS black hole, and explores its non-equilibrium process of shadow evolution under perturbation. The research reveals that a stronger non-linearity parameter results in a larger black hole shadow and a more rapid decrease in temperature, indicating a stronger connection between geometric and thermal properties. In addition, the study analyzes the phase structure of the nonlinear charged AdS black hole and finds multiple steady states under specific parameter conditions. It also reveals that black holes with larger radii experience a more significant shadow reduction and a more rapid temperature increase following a size increment. These findings contribute to our understanding of the relationship between thermal and geometric properties in black hole physics.

Following the principles introduced by Landau and Lifshitz in 1962, we explore the presentation of two key quantum phenomena - the violation of an equality and the breakdown of an principle at the output of a beam splitter using Wigner and Radon tomograms.

Following the discovery of $B_{s}^0$ mixing, a new analysis is conducted to determine if the observed $\bar{D}^0$ in the final state of $B_{s}^0$ decays results from direct production or $B_{s}^0$ oscillation, given that both $B_{d}^0$ and $B_{s}^0$ oscillate at different rates. Utilizing a 3.0 $\text{TeV}^{-1}$ dataset collected by the LHCb detector, which comprises 11 million $B_{s}^0$ mesons, no confirmed cases of $B_{s}^0\to K^0_S D^{*-0}$ and a limited number of $B_{s}^0\to K^0_S \bar{D}^0$ mesons were identified, with possible background events potentially attributed to $B_{d}^0\to K^0_S \bar{D}^0$ decays and a potential unconfirmed instance of $B_{s}^0\to K^0_S \bar{D}^{*0}$, yielding updated lower confidence interval limits.

A module over a group is considered lattice polytope in certain cases, where calculating the lattice of submodules becomes equivalent to determining the vertices of the lattice polytope. In contrast, for modules with no mass function, calculating the lattice of submodules remains a challenging task, particularly when dealing with extensive composition series data. A breakthrough occurs when working with modules over a group where the composition series are concise; in this context, an efficient algorithm has been developed to construct the lattice of submodules from the provided data. This approach is illustrated with an application to representation theory, specifically in determining the lattice of invariant subspaces for a specific module associated with the symmetric group $S_7$, reducing its invariance factors in comparison to previous methods applied to larger modules over $S_5$ and $S_6$.

We explore how several operators including several specialized functions such as curvature and shape affect a specific type of geometric configuration known as biharmonic hypersurfaces within a particular space called Euclidean space. As a result, we identify several characteristics of this configuration. Additionally, we focus on a particular type of behavior known as recurring for both the shape and curvature of the configuration, proving that this behavior is equivalent to another set of similar behaviors including semi-exact and exactly invariant. With this understanding, we deduce the precise form of the specified behavior for the mentioned configurations.

This research ascertains that a previously proposed $p/q$-identifiable concept by Ju and Thiel results in a special case of the more broadly applicable p/q-visible concept introduced by Thiel. Consequently, the Ju-Thiel finding indicates that an ideal point-function pair constitutes a particularly distinct form of p/q-visible ideal pair.

Following the measured data for $B_s^0\rightarrow D_s^{*-}\mu^{+}\nu_{\mu}$ decays, we conduct a shape analysis of the differential decay rate, focusing on both the $B_s^0$ and $D_s^{*-}$ meson polarizations. Comparing theoretical predictions with recent CDF results, we assess the form factor models' fidelity. Based on these model comparisons, we derive constraints on their parameters. Additionally, utilizing input from form factor models that align with the data, we estimate the $B_s^0\rightarrow D_s^{-}mu^{+}nu_{\mu}$ decay rate.

A persistent rumor suggests that tearing an adhesive strip in two results in a sound pattern governed by fundamental physics, potentially revealing a concealed arrangement of fractures governed by power laws and clustering tendencies. We confirm the existence of clustering in adhesive strip testing through both image analysis and mathematical modeling, contrasting it with the disordered sound emission patterns observed, possibly influenced by rapid fracture speeds. Although theoretical considerations indicate a power law distribution of crack sizes, our high-speed camera observations reveal a bimodal pattern, contradicting the assumed size distribution. Consequently, acoustic emission data alone may not be sufficient to accurately depict the underlying physical processes at work.

In 1930s, Menger developed the concept of an angle space and defined several properties within this framework. By the1950s, Menger summarized three unresolved problems related to this framework, though only two remainunsolved currently. This paper aims to resolve the remaining two unresolved problems by redefining the initial specifications in terms of a generated partial order closure operator, and verifying that the resulting angle space properties areequivalent to previously established representational conditions. These new conditions exhibit stronger connectivity tothe mathematical theory of generated closure operators. Additionally, we provide concrete counter-examples to threepotential representational conditions from the existing literature.

Point cloud data used in point recognition tasks often undergoes various transformations like rotation, scaling, and translation prior to analysis. The purpose of these preprocessing steps is to enhance the effectiveness of point cloud representations used in recognition tasks. Currently, there isn't a universally accepted method for creating representations that are invariant to these transformations. This lack of a standard approach hinders the development and comparison of point cloud-based recognition systems. To address this issue, we propose a novel representation called Transformation-Dependent Smoothing (TPC), designed to facilitate the efficiency of point recognition tasks. Our experiments on multiple dataset showing that our TPC method outperforms existing state-of-the-art smoothing techniques, leading to significant improvements in performance. Specifically, our proposed representation results in 85.4%, 90.1%, and 82.8% accuracy on Model, Object, and Scene datasets respectively, representing substantial gains over existing methods. The success of our TPC approach demonstrates its potential effectiveness in creating efficient and accurate point cloud-based recognition systems.

The structure of a program can be represented as a geometric shape, specifically a lattice, where the top and bottom points correspond to non-functional programs and the immediate next levels represent simplified versions of the program, such as its syntax tree and control flow graph. The middle section of this lattice is of particular interest, excluding the top and bottom points and the adjacent levels. In a recent study, we investigate the relevance of defect testing in automating the verification of user-defined properties. Our findings show that testing specific points in this section of the lattice is equivalent to measuring local changes in the geometric shape of the lattice resulting from those tests. This local defect testing can be extended to a more comprehensive, global defect testing method by utilizing an existing, automatic program rewriting tool. The resulting global testing is equivalent to measuring the overall geometric deformation of the lattice caused by the rewriting tool after testing various points. The significance of this equivalence lies in the potential for using geometric methods to enhance the efficiency of global testing in various applications.

We provide a novel application of Kummer theory to establish $p$-adic unit conditions previously identified by Serre and Clear for GL_2, replacing the original field theoretic arguments. Specifically, we demonstrate that the conditions imposed by Kummer theory on the eigenspaces of an eigenvariety's tangent space correspond to those established by Serre and Clear, ensuring the existence of certain "Serre weights." This approach is particularly advantageous as it bypasses the need for higher-dimensional representations, which may not always be accessible, and instead relies on the availability of square roots of a fourth power eigenvalue, which is generally more accessible.

The internal structure of composite materials with a matrix embedded with conductive particles can be precisely determined through electrical impedance tomography (EIT). This method provides a non-destructive way to image the distribution of stresses within these materials. To enhance the quality of these images, an EVolutionary Algorithm for COntour refinement (ERCO) was developed. This algorithm uses initial EIT images to create more accurate electrical conductivity models of the material's internal structure. A 2D simulation demonstrated the effectiveness of this combination, with an improvement in image resolution from FIG. 1 to 2. This level of detail allows for a precise description of the material's internal shape using just five coefficients in a polynomial, as shown in FIG. 3. This capability opens up new possibilities for using EIT to monitor changes in the internal structure of self-sensing composites in real-time in response to external forces.

This study explores a novel tensorial approach to Euclidean geometry by explicitly defining and proving key geometric concepts such as distance, angle, and volume within a $n$-dimensional Euclidean space using tensor operations. Notably, this method utilizes the geometric properties of both Euclidean space and its dual space, as well as a specific $2$-rank geometric tensor to establish the foundations of Euclidean geometry. Furthermore, this framework can be extended to define similar geometric concepts in non-Euclidean spaces, particularly in the context of general relativity.

If a right-angled Artin group (RAAG) associated with a graph G undergoes a non-trivial divergence-inducing division under an action of the group on a building, the corresponding invariant in the flag complex of the building corresponds to a cycle within the fundamental cycle complex of the group. This holds particularly so for 2-dimensional buildings.

The need for real-time image processing and optimization in large-scale machine learning models has grown significantly, creating a demand for efficient iterative matrix inversion methods.  This paper introduces a novel approach called Generalized Advanced Order (GAO) techniques, an extension of the goby techniques originally proposed in 2016.  The goby techniques are applicable to symmetric positive semi-definite matrices, while the GAO methods overcome this limitation and can handle matrices with complex eigenvalues.  Building on this foundation, the paper also presents an even more versatile technique called Multi-dimensional GAO (MGAO), designed to further accelerate matrix inversion processes by utilizing multiple simultaneous goby steps in each iteration.  Experimental results demonstrate that the GAO and MGAO methods outperform both the goby techniques and the original goby methods in terms of both accuracy and speed, making them highly suitable for applications requiring real-time matrix inversion in large matrices.  The GAO and MGAO techniques are particularly valuable for constructing precise surrogates of Hessian matrices in large-scale machine learning optimization tasks, as well as processing high-definition videos and medical images in real-time.

Situational linear bandits is a framework commonly used to represent and make decisions in real-world applications such as content recommendation and advertising. A key characteristic of this dynamic environment is its contextual nature, where the set of available options may vary from one situation to another, presenting a challenge known as missing data. Existing solutions often focus on specific types of situations, leaving a gap in understanding more complex scenarios. This research aims to bridge this gap by developing efficient algorithms for situations where the option set is randomly determined, along with a theoretically-backed performance metric. The proposed methods demonstrate a strong balance between accuracy and computational costs, outperforming previous approaches in both simulated and actual data settings, showcasing their practical significance.

A phenomenon observed recently where a protoplanetary disk's acceleration and turbulence in its outer areas gets triggered by a dust storm has its connection to the wind speed's relationship with the disk's rotation rate, or $\nu$, explored in this study's analysis of instability in such scenarios.

This research focuses on proving a theorem by Liouville regarding the stability of Ricci curvature from the perspective of geometric probability processes. The proof utilizes the theory of $p$-变数几何概率过程 to demonstrate that if a Riemannian manifold has a bounded geometric probability process with a constant value for its curvature in 2维 and its Ricci curvature does not increase, then its geometry must be flat. This proof is particularly relevant for geometric probability processes with a specific value of $p$ greater than or equal to 49510400000000000000000000000000.

This study presents a novel configuration for a convolutional neural network, consisting of a dynamic arrangement of sub-networks that pool their outputs at the end. Each sub-network utilizes a distinct set of features, specifically utilizing shared back-end components while employing independent front-end components. The number of features utilized in each sub-network can be adjusted during training and inference, allowing the network to adapt its configuration based on the input data in real-time. This approach eliminates the need for fixed configurations of convolutions or aggregations, enabling a more efficient use of resources and a greater flexibility in processing images with varying levels of detail. Our method, VETNet, achieves state-of-the-line results on several image super-resolution datasets, including DIV2K, FIQA, and MOSAIC, and also explores the relationship between the number of features utilized in each sub-network and the performance of the model, revealing that optimal results are not necessarily achieved with the highest resolution possible.

Educations such as machines learning systems often struggle to keep up with the varying concepts and vocabularies found in data from different sources, especially when new data arrives continuously. Federated learning technologies help protect user data privacy but can be hindered by the efficiency losses caused by its iterative nature. This paper presents a novel, information-centric federated learning scheme called DME-FL to overcame these challenges by leveraging random exploration strategies to ensure concept coverage while maintaining data privacy. Our results show that this approach outperforms existing methods in maintaining learning quality while significantly accelerating the process.

A novel consistency regularization method called AWKWARD has been presented and demonstrated to be highly effective in the domain of medical image segmentation. This deeply iterative algorithm works by alternating between an inner optimization step that updates segmentations and an outer optimization step that updates a neural network. Its effectiveness is illustrated through experiments on several publicly available datasets, showing state-of-the-line results without relying on graph-based or manual correction methods.

A persistent controversy exists in the field of quantum physics over the ability of single-particle states to exhibit true nonlocal phenomena. Some researchers argue that since a single particle cannot be divided into parts, it cannot display nonlocality, thus deeming discussions on the topic to be meaningless. In contrast, I present original work demonstrating that single-particle entanglement can indeed produce genuine nonlocal effects, disproving the notion that one-particle wavefunctions are merely mathematical constructs without physical significance. These findings suggest that the debate over the nonlocality of single-particle states and its relevance to EPR correlations is misdirected. Instead, the crucial factor lying ahead for a more in-depth comprehension of these phenomena is the origin of single-particle entanglement, which arises from the nonlocal nature of quantum fields. This nonlocality enables a distinct form of guidance, facilitating the establishment of local interactions at detection points, analogous to the role of the pilot wave in de Broglie-Bohm theory. Drawing on dephased density matrices that erase single-particle entanglement and nonlocality, it becomes evident that this entity plays a crucial role in registering measurement outcomes. Consequently, the research on the local effects exhibited by single-particle states can be regarded as a contemporary reinterpretation of de Broglie-Bohm theory tailored to quantum fields.

The integration of self-managing and privacy-focused technologies like Blockchain and Federated Learning has gained significant traction in Internet of Vehicles (IoVs) Education systems to enhance data security and optimize information dissemination. The IoVs environment, characterized by its dynamic and open nature, frequently encounters issues such as malicious behavior, data inconsistency, and limited system resources. Conversely, the IoVs Education Framework, designed to promote safe and effective driving, continues to evolve with emerging technologies, adapting to new information needs and advancements in IoVs systems. This paper provides an in-depth examination of various Blockchain and Federated Learning-based solutions that have been developed to address these challenges, exploring their technical implementations, advantages, disadvantages, and potential improvements. Moreover, the document outlines several promising directions for future research in this domain, including the design of more efficient and secure protocols, the development of scalable and adaptable systems, and the creation of robust evaluation metrics. By synthesizing the latest innovations in Blockchain and Federated Learning technologies, this work offers a comprehensive roadmap for designing sophisticated and effective IoVs Education Frameworks in real-world scenarios, informing policymakers, system developers, and researchers about potential strategies for optimizing traffic flow, enhancing safety, and mitigating accidents through customized IoVs Education content.

Deep learning models such as LSTMs excel in processing sequential data but suffer from slow computation and large sizes, particularly when implemented using hardware. In contrast, shallow models like GRUs and RNNs are more efficient for hardware implementation but may not fully capture the complexities of sequential data. Our work presents a combined approach that utilizes Tensor Decomposition to optimize the implementation of LSTM networks on hardware, allowing for accurate video identification while significantly reducing computation and memory requirements. Our designed LSTM accelerator achieves real-time video identification with far field acoustic feedback, demonstrating an accuracy of 86.8% on the SSR dataset and enabling end-to-end video classification with a high frame rate of 1000fps, achieving an accuracy of 87.0% on the Grid dataset. This work has significant implications for the development of intelligent and energy-efficient hardware systems.

This study delves into the concept of iterated combinations of polynomials. Let $f$ and $g$ be complex-coefficient polynomials in one variable, where the degree of $f$ is at least 2. The composition $f_n$ is obtained by repeatedly applying $f$ to it $n$ times, with $f_0$ being the identity function, and similarly, the composition $h_m$ is obtained by repeatedly applying the function $g_h$ to it $m$ times. The article positives the following theorems: (1) When the degrees of $f_n(g_m(x))$ and $f_n(g_m(cx+d))$ are both at least 2, if the difference between them has a degree less than the minimum of their respective degrees, then $g$ is a linear function; (2) When the degrees of $f_n(g_m(x))$ and $f_{n-1}(g_{m-1}(cx+d))$ are both at least 2, the conditions for $g$ to be a linear function are also met.

This paper examines solutions to the Schrödinger equation under specific initial and boundary conditions, focusing on scenarios where "explosion" or instantaneous singularities might occur. Utilizing the Hartree-Fock approximation, we investigate the influence of boundary shapes on these singularities, hypothesizing that convex boundaries inhibit their formation. To investigate this, we carry out numerical simulations with both Gaussian and non-Gaussian initial conditions, employing a high-order spectral method combined with a symplectic time-stepping approach. Our results reveal that while concave boundaries promote explosions, their occurrence is also influenced by initial conditions and energy levels. Furthermore, we observe that lower-dimensional boundaries reduce the likelihood of explosions, and the presence of multiple concave areas increases the likelihood of their occurrence.
Following the notation of [14], we define a local, descriptive model for variety reduction.

Hypothesis testing methods in statistics often face criticism for their frequentist leanings, with Bayes factors proposed as a more informative alternative. Although calculating Bayes factors can be computationally demanding, especially in complex models, we demonstrate that it's feasible to do so with modern hardware. Our research identifies key elements required for successful Bayes factor calculations and proposes a flexible framework consisting of three main approaches: batch processing, interactive exploration, and sequential planning. This adaptive multiple testing strategy allows researchers to achieve extremely low p-values in Bayes factor testing without significant computational resources, making it applicable to large datasets. We illustrate the effectiveness of this framework using several examples, including a simple coin toss scenario, a well-known dataset, a real-world data set, and a cosmological model. Notably, we optimize a parameter set in a cosmic neutrino mass dataset from a large experiment by a factor of ten with minimal computational effort in a single node. We believe this systematic approach will benefit both statisticians and data analysts, potentially influencing the design of future studies and analyses.

Recent advances in NLP have led to more complex models with numerous components, such as neural networks that utilize various discourse indicators. Despite their significance in facilitating meaningful interactions between model components, existing datasets used for training and evaluating these models often lack sufficient semantic labels, resulting in random assignments of discourse indicators. This method often proves ineffective, particularly when the models are deployed in real-world scenarios. To address this issue, we introduce the first large-scale, high-quality semantic discourse dataset, consisting of 16 categories and 119 sub-categories, designed specifically for English discourse indicators. This dataset, which includes explanations for each indicator, can be utilized to train semantic discourse models, as well as evaluate and analyze both existing and new discourse indicators in a specified context. Applying this framework to a pre-existing model, we were able to significantly enhance the Berkeley Advisor Agent's performance by 17% on the SVAB task, demonstrating the potential benefits of training and utilizing semantic discourse models. Furthermore, we conducted a detailed evaluation of the dataset by training a training and evaluating a deep learning model to classify discourse indicators, resulting in substantial improvements over the original annotations.

Recently introduced is the concept of a twist within the Jordanian frame, a special type of deformation operator, and subsequently, the Jordanian twisted quantum Smorodinsky model, a specific application of this framework. By extending this model, we derive the Smorodinsky-like model adapted to the Jordanian frame, laying the groundwork for applying the twist in analogous situations.

This study develops an algorithm for addressing inequality problems with extended regular expressions, which represent language sets, in a symbolic manner, and utilizes automata theory to translate these expressions into models for analysis. We incorporate new features, such as subset and superset operators, into the algorithm and demonstrate its practical application through various tests, comparing its performance with existing methods, and present statistical analysis of the results obtained.

Building upon previous work (arXiv:1601.00507, arXiv:1701.01504), we derive a complete set of tree-level four-point functions for a specific type of conformal field theory module to satisfy the massless Bethe-Salpeger equation in AdS space. This is achieved by applying the AdS/CFT correspondence and utilizing the bulk four-point function expression in terms of scalar block expansions. We demonstrate the equivalence between the BMN expansion and the Berenstein-Duffing formalism for a particular CFT module representing a large spin primary field in two dimensions. Furthermore, we confirm the validity of the BMN expansion and related integral equations derived previously (arXiv:1104.3731) when applied to this specific case.

To maximize the wide field of view achieved by lobster-eye (LE) designs, a novel configuration called multiplexed lobster-eye (MuLE) has been proposed. This setup involves arranging multiple LE segments, each with a slightly offset central axis, around a common focal point within a multi-layered structure. An example design called TRIPOD, consisting of three LE modules, is outlined with specific dimensions and material requirements. Simulation results using MCPLX show that a three-module setup can maintain high detection efficiency while preserving the wide field of view offered by LE technology. Furthermore, expanding the number of modules in an LE design offers advantages over traditional single-module configurations, allowing for larger active areas and reduced costs per square inch.

To predict the distribution of dark matter halos, a deep learning method is proposed to process the large-scale structure of the universe as input.  After training on a synthetic dataset generated by simulations, a variant of the Message Passing Neural Network (MP-NN) called D2-MSG-NN demonstrated exceptional accuracy in recreating the halo mass function, closely matching the results from full simulations.  Notably, the required dark matter resolution is five times greater than that of the initial scale of the random walk process, allowing for an efficient computation of the halo mass function through simulations.  Furthermore, the input representation of the field responsible for halo collapse as a feature in the D2-MSG-NN model indicates its correlation with halo formation.  Consequently, the model can classify dark and normal matter particles based on their properties and even predict halo locations with high precision.  To verify the validity of this conclusion, a simplified one-dimensional model of halo collapse has been developed and analyzed, confirming the halo formation's dependence on the local density, velocity, and the Hubble parameter, with the cosmic speed field playing a more significant role than previously thought.  Based on these findings, the model suggests the halo mass function's universal nature may originate from the halo formation's reliance on the local density, velocity, and Hubble parameter, with the cosmic speed field contributing uniquely to this process.  This discovery potentially paves the way for a dark halo phase space function simulation in a near-future large-scale
